passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Funeral services were held for Michael and Mary.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Their daughter had not been located. The investigation continued as the family buried Jennifer’s parents without knowing whether Jennifer was still alive.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: A new search warrant revealed a.22-caliber pistol was removed from the Short home, in addition to other weapons.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Strong Lead Fails to Develop: Investigators received what Sheriff Frank Cassell characterized as a strong lead. Detectives pursued the information.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: It ultimately failed to produce the hoped-for breakthrough.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Ten days after Jennifer disappeared, some investigators received their first meaningful break from the investigation after working extremely long hours.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Sheriff Cassell said at least four investigators would remain assigned to the case. The strong lead received Friday night had not panned out.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities continued expressing hope that Jennifer might be found alive.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: DNA testing had also been conducted concerning whether Michael and Mary were Jennifer’s biological parents. Cassell said they had received the results but declined to release them publicly.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities said they still had no suspect. The reward had reached approximately $11,000.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police received information concerning a possible stalker of Mary Short from when she worked at Pluma in 1992

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman’s landlord reportedly told authorities that Bowman had made statements about wanting or threatening to kill a Virginia mobile-home mover following a dispute involving the movement of a mobile home. Michael Short operated a mobile-home moving company.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: First Investigation of Garrison Bowman: Law enforcement received information concerning Garrison Bowman.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators searched property associated with Bowman. The FBI interviewed Bowman during August.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: At this stage, investigators did not publicly establish that Bowman and Michael Short had actually been involved in the dispute described by the informant. That distinction later became important.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police exhumed Michael Short’s body for additional forensic testing.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Postal officials initially denied investigators access to the Shorts’ mail. The issue was subsequently resolved. By then the reward exceeded $50,000.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The warrants were based partly on statements from Rick Lemons concerning Bowman’s alleged threats and activities shortly before the murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators searched Bowman’s former residence and collected evidence for testing.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities obtained search warrants connected to Bowman.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police scaled down physical searches. Police said they would conduct no additional land, helicopter, or dive searches unless new information justified them.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Police released 10-year-old photographs of Mary Short hoping to generate information about the alleged Pluma “stalker” incident.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer’s aunt and uncle, Ruby and Chris Young, were named her legal guardians if she was found.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman’s landlord returned to the Short residence and spoke with investigators.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Albert’s daughter, Lisa Albert, told The Roanoke Times that the family’s dogs had been seen tossing around what initially looked like a brown wig in the driveway.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: After authorities arrived, investigators discovered teeth and bone fragments scattered around the yard.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: A subsequent foot search of the surrounding property located a section of ribs in a shallow stream bed and a cluster of bone fragments in a small pond behind the residence.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Detectives began dragging the pond to determine whether additional remains were underwater.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Cadaver dogs from the Triad Bloodhound Team in Forsyth County, North Carolina, were brought in to search the surrounding woods. The dogs found no additional bones that day.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: 1:30 p.m. Human Remains Discovered: A small human skull with hair still attached was discovered at the property of Eddie Albert on Grogan Road in Stoneville, Rockingham County, North Carolina, approximately 30 minutes south of Oak Level, Virginia.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Later: The search was suspended at sunset and scheduled to resume the following morning.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Henry County investigators obtained a hair sample from the skull and other evidence and transported the material to Roanoke, where Jennifer’s belongings were being held, in an attempt to make a preliminary comparison.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: At that point, neither Virginia nor North Carolina authorities would publicly identify the remains as Jennifer’s. Rockingham County Sheriff Sam Page said he could neither confirm nor rule it out, while Henry County Sheriff Frank Cassell said he was doubtful but acknowledged they did not yet know.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators also checked a Civil War-era cemetery near the Albert property to determine whether any graves had been disturbed. Deputies found no evidence of disturbed graves.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities planned to compare the discovery against missing-person cases within a 50-mile radius.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: An unusual detail Sheriff Cassell noted was that the Henry County Sheriff’s Office initially learned about the discovery from a North Carolina news organization rather than North Carolina law enforcement. Cassell said this made him suspicious, although a Rockingham County Sheriff’s Office spokesperson suggested local authorities may simply have wanted to determine what they were dealing with before contacting Virginia investigators.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The remains were scheduled to be transported to the North Carolina state medical examiner’s office in Chapel Hill for examination.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Contemporary reporting stated that Jennifer’s remains were discovered approximately one-half mile to one mile from a mobile home Bowman had occupied or owned before leaving for Canada. Different contemporary accounts gave slightly different distance estimates.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: This proximity led investigators to take a second, closer look at Bowman.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Connection to Bowman Property: The location of Jennifer’s remains attracted renewed attention to Garrison Bowman.
